title: Homogeneous ideal of a closed subscheme of projective space over a ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$, and $B=R[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ with each variable of degree one. Let $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_R=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-proj]. For each $d\geq0$ define $I_d\subseteq B_d$ to consist of the homogeneous polynomials $F$ such that, for every $0\leq i\leq n$, the regular function $F/z_i^d$ on $D_+(z_i)$ restricts to zero on the open subscheme $Z\cap D_+(z_i)$; here $D_+(z_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{(z_i),0})$ is the standard affine chart [def-pc-proj]. Then $I=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}I_d$ is a homogeneous ideal of $B$, and the canonical closed immersion $\operatorname{Proj}(B/I)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ identifies $\operatorname{Proj}(B/I)$ with $Z$ as a closed subscheme. Neither reducedness nor nonemptiness of $Z$ is required.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space (I_d is the kernel of R[T_0,...,T_n]_d -> Gamma(Z, O(d)|_Z); here expressed in the standard trivializations on D_+(z_i)).

proof.text: For every $d$, the set $I_d$ is an $R$-submodule of $B_d$: restriction of $(F+G)/z_i^d$ is the sum of the restrictions and restriction commutes with scalar multiplication. For $F\in I_d$ and $H\in B_e$, the equality $(HF)/z_i^{d+e}=(H/z_i^e)(F/z_i^d)$ shows $HF\in I_{d+e}$. Every polynomial is a finite sum of homogeneous components, so distributing multiplication proves that $I=\bigoplus_d I_d$ is an ideal; its definition as this direct sum proves homogeneity. Give $C=B/I$ the quotient grading $C_d=B_d/I_d$.

Put $C=B/I$. The surjective-map clause (3) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] gives a closed immersion $Z'=\operatorname{Proj}(C)\hookrightarrow P$. The chart formula of [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] identifies its preimage of $U_a=D_+(z_a)$ with $D_+(\bar z_a)$, induced by $q_a:F/z_a^d\mapsto\bar F/\bar z_a^d$. The $U_a$ cover by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open], since the variables generate $B_+$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $Z\cap U_a=\operatorname{Spec}(A_a/J_a)$, where $A_a=B_{(z_a),0}$ and $J_a$ is the restriction kernel.

Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-quotient-chart-kernel] to $S=B$, $K=I$, $f=z_a$. It identifies $C_{(\bar z_a),0}$ over $A_a$ with $A_a/J'_a$, where $J'_a$ is generated by $F/z_a^d$ for $F\in I_d$. Each generator lies in $J_a$ by the definition of $I_d$. Conversely, for $f\in J_a$, [lem-sfb-projective-local-equation-extension] supplies $G=z_a^NF\in B_{d+N}$ vanishing on every $Z\cap U_j$ and satisfying $f=G/z_a^{d+N}$. Thus $G\in I_{d+N}$, so $f\in J'_a$. Hence $J'_a=J_a$ on every chart.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space (I_d is the kernel of R[T_0,...,T_n]_d -> Gamma(Z, O(d)|_Z); here expressed in the standard trivializations on D_+(z_i)).

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I_Z,\mathcal I_{Z'}\subseteq\mathcal O_P$ be the ideal sheaves of the closed immersions $Z\hookrightarrow P$ and $Z'\hookrightarrow P$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. On each affine chart $U_a$ their ideals of sections are $\mathcal I_Z(U_a)=J_a$, by the definition of $J_a$ in Step 2, and $\mathcal I_{Z'}(U_a)=\ker(q_a)=J'_a$, since Step 2 identifies $Z'\cap U_a\to U_a$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(q_a)$ and Step 3 computes the kernel. By Step 3, $J_a=J'_a$, so [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] gives $\mathcal I_Z|_{U_a}=\widetilde{J_a}=\mathcal I_{Z'}|_{U_a}$ for every $a$. The $U_a$ cover $P$ (Step 2), and whether a section of $\mathcal O_P$ lies in a subsheaf can be checked locally, so $\mathcal I_Z=\mathcal I_{Z'}$. Then [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] gives a unique morphism $Z'\to Z$ over $P$, and it is an isomorphism. This identifies $\operatorname{Proj}(B/I)$ with $Z$ as a closed subscheme of $P$. Nothing here uses reducedness, nonemptiness of $Z$ or $R\neq0$: a chart that misses $Z$ has $J_a=A_a$ on both sides.
